To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the specification of cell fate in petals involves the action of transcription factors that are expressed in a spatially restricted manner.

(1) the transcription factor MIXTA is required for the specification of conical cells and trichomes; (2) MIXTA is activated late in petal differentiation, and its activity is restricted to inner epidermal cells by its specific expression pattern; (3) the expression of MIXTA is regulated by the B-function genes DEFICIENS, SEPALLATA and GLOBOSA; and (4) the expression of AmMYBML2 may be required for the formation or
MIXTA specifies the formation of conically shaped epidermal cells in Antirrinum petals, and that MIXTA is activated by B-function genes in the late petal developmental program.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic control of cell fate in the petals of Antirrhinun majus.
how the expression of a single gene can specify different cell fated in different cell types.
the mechanisms that control the specification of cell fates in petals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epidermal cells are determined by a series of transcription factors, and the cell fate is determined by the expression of these transcription factors.
cell fate determination in the petals is regulated by the interaction of transcription factors and their targets.
the regulatory genes that specify cell fates are not necessarily the same in all organs, but they do have a common origin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the specification of different cell types within the petals is controlled by a hierarchy of transcription factors.
the formation of different cell types within the same tissue is achieved through the differential expression of genes which are members of a family.
the cell fate of the cells of the epidermis is specified by the combination of the regulatory gene activity and the timing and localization of expression of these regulatory genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell fate determination is a complex process, involving multiple regulatory genes.
the specification of cell fates is a dynamic process, with the same gene having different functions in different cell types.
the same regulatory network can direct the formation of different cell types.
